---
title: "Visium, HD bins and segmented-cell workflows"
---

SCOP uses Seurat as the user-facing container. Choose a workflow according to
the observation unit and the biological question. A bin is not automatically a
cell, and expression clusters do not automatically define anatomical domains.

| Input | Recommended entry | Additional decisions |
|---|---|---|
| Visium spots | `ReadSpatialData(..., "visium")` and `RunStandardWorkflow()` | Spatial QC, domains, reference-dependent deconvolution |
| Visium HD bins | `ReadSpatialData(..., "visium_hd")` and `RunSpatialSketch()` | Explicit resolution; sampling and projection; bin-level interpretation |
| Xenium cells | `ReadSpatialData(..., "xenium")`, `SpatialSegmentationQC()` | Segmentation quality, annotation and cell neighborhoods |

These examples use real vendor output directories that the user supplies. They
are not executed during a documentation build. No loader installs dependencies
or downloads data. Seurat's supported file formats and version remain the
loader boundary; CosMx/MERSCOPE import is not implemented by this new loader.
Existing Seurat objects from other supported loaders can use the downstream
functions with explicit observation types and units.

## Visium: choose the existing methods through one workflow

```r
spatial <- ReadSpatialData("path/to/visium/outs", "visium", sample_id = "S1")
SpatialDataInfo(spatial, assay = "Spatial", image = "slice1")

spatial <- RunStandardWorkflow(
  spatial, workflow = "spatial", assay = "Spatial", image = "slice1",
  do_spatial_qc = TRUE,
  spatial_qc_params = list(run_artifact = FALSE),
  do_spatial_cluster = TRUE,
  spatial_cluster_method = "BANKSY",
  spatial_cluster_params = list(lambda = 0.2, resolution = 0.6),
  do_deconvolution = FALSE
)
spatial@tools$run_standard_spatial_workflow$stages
SpatialSpotPlot(spatial, group.by = "BANKSY_cluster", image = "slice1")
```

Here SpotSweeper runs local QC, with artifact detection explicitly not requested.
It does not remove observations. When artifact detection is requested but cannot
complete, the stage fails with the stage table attached to the error; a partial
artifact assessment is not reported as a completed workflow.

For SmoothClust, use `spatial_cluster_method = "SmoothClust"`, `spatial_q = 4`
and `spatial_cluster_params = list(smooth_method = "knn", k = 18)`. For BANKSY,
use its resolution parameter instead of `spatial_q`. Existing BayesSpace calls
and `bayesspace_params` remain supported; do not supply both parameter lists.
HD bin input routes BayesSpace to its `VisiumHD` platform unless explicitly
overridden in method parameters. Segmented cells are rejected by the BayesSpace
and spot-deconvolution branches of the standard workflow.

## Keep normalized expression separate from counts

```r
normalized <- RunStandardWorkflow(
  spatial, workflow = "spatial", assay = "Spatial", image = "slice1",
  normalization_method = "SpaNorm",
  spanorm_params = list(new_assay = "SpaNormAnalysis"),
  do_spatial_cluster = TRUE, spatial_cluster_method = "BANKSY",
  do_deconvolution = FALSE
)
normalized@tools$run_standard_spatial_workflow$parameters
```

The input assay remains the count source for deconvolution and BayesSpace.
SpaNorm writes a separate normalized assay used for expression preprocessing,
Moran/Geary features, BANKSY and SmoothClust. The default HVF method switches
from count-based `vst` to data-based `mvp` for the SpaNorm output. The workflow
also attaches the matching original counts to that assay for library QC; these
are never replaced with normalized values. Explicit
method parameter overrides are retained. Count-based SVG backends must receive
an appropriate original assay/layer explicitly. Selecting SpaNorm with
`do_normalization = FALSE` is rejected; a preexisting destination assay also
requires choosing a new name.

## Visium HD: preserve resolutions and full-data identity

Seurat's [HD workflow](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/visiumhd_analysis_vignette)
stores multiple resolutions in separate assays/images. SCOP preserves this
structure and records bin size separately from coordinate units: an 8-micron
bin can still have image coordinates expressed in full-resolution pixels.

```r
hd <- ReadSpatialData("path/to/hd/outs", "visium_hd",
                      bin.size = c(8, 16), sample_id = "HD1")
SpatialDataInfo(hd, assay = "Spatial.008um", image = "slice1.008um")
hd <- RunSpatialSketch(
  hd, assay = "Spatial.008um", image = "slice1.008um",
  ncells = 50000, nfeatures = 2000, npcs = 30,
  method = "LeverageScore", prefix = "HD8"
)
hd@tools$HD8$summary
SpatialSpotPlot(hd, image = "slice1.008um", group.by = "HD8_projected")
saveRDS(hd, "hd-analysis.rds")
reloaded <- readRDS("hd-analysis.rds")
SpatialDataInfo(reloaded, assay = "Spatial.008um", image = "slice1.008um")
```

The full count matrix remains sparse if it was sparse on input. Only sampled
cells are scaled. The memory guard estimates the sketch's scaled matrix; it
does not promise a bound on total memory, and arbitrary on-disk matrix backends
have not all been certified. The workflow records sampled and projected cells
separately and rejects conflicting output names. A single observed sketch
cluster receives a constant full-data label, explicitly recorded in provenance.
This case does not support claims about multiple tissue populations.

An assay spanning multiple independent images must be subset to the intended
image context before sketching. This prevents accidentally sampling an unrelated
section. Physical image registration and cross-section 3D reconstruction are
separate analyses, not implied by expression projection or PRECAST integration.

For spatial feature detection, the C++ Moran/Geary and SPARK-X paths retain
sparse input. R-reference and nnSVG conversions check `max_dense_gb` before
materializing a dense expression matrix. Reduce the requested features instead
of increasing this limit blindly. Inspect the exact input assay/layer.

## Xenium: audit real segmentation and retain full neighborhood context

```r
cells <- ReadSpatialData("path/to/xenium/outs", "xenium", sample_id = "X1")
info <- SpatialDataInfo(cells, assay = "Xenium", image = "fov")
qc <- SpatialSegmentationQC(cells, assay = "Xenium", image = "fov")
head(qc)
SpatialCellPlot(cells, image = "fov", features = rownames(cells)[1],
                assay = "Xenium", layer = "counts")
```

Polygon area is an area of the supplied boundary representation, not a new
segmentation or a claim to recover the original pixel mask. Vendor polygons
can simplify the underlying segmentation. Missing polygons produce missing
area and `not_evaluated`, never a synthetic circle or an automatic pass. Supply
`min_counts` and/or `area_range` only after inspecting the tissue and acquisition.
Multi-ring tables require explicit logical `hole` values for area calculation.
No threshold filters the object automatically.

After annotating cell types in `celltype`, profile target cells while preserving
surrounding tissue:

```r
profile <- SpatialNeighborhoodProfile(
  cells, group.by = "celltype", image = "fov",
  radii = c(25, 50, 100), sample.by = "spatial_sample",
  cells = colnames(cells)[cells$celltype == "T cell"]
)
```

Radii here are microns only because the Xenium loader's provenance records
micron coordinates. A metadata-only Seurat object otherwise has unknown units.
The profile measures observed neighborhood composition, without a tissue-edge
correction or a contact/communication claim. See [sample comparisons](spatial-sample-comparisons.html)
for aggregation across independent subjects.

## Reproducible validation

`scripts/validate-spatial-platforms.R` runs public fixtures in isolated R
processes, records errors and sampled process-tree peak memory, saves results,
reloads them, and renders their stored outputs. Optional backends are recorded
as unavailable instead of being installed automatically. The companion
`scripts/spatial-platform-data.md` records download sources and intended scope.
Mock adapter tests are separate from these live integration runs. Small
developer fixtures validate formats and computation, not biological performance
on complete production slides.
